resolvit: resolvō, -ere, -solvī, -solūtum — to loosen, untie, undo, unbind (3rd sg. pres.; also 3rd sg. perf.)
respondet: respondeō, -ēre, -spondī, -sponsum — to answer, reply; correspond to (3rd sg. pres.)
revoluta: revolvō, -ere, -volvī, -volūtum — to roll back, turn back (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; revoluta est, she rolled back)
sacrum: sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, holy (n. acc. sg.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
satis: satis (indecl. n., adv.) — enough, sufficient; adv., sufficiently
secreta: sēcernō, -ere, sēcrēvī, sēcrētum — to set apart; sēcrētus, -a, -um, apart, secluded (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (secreta in sede, in a secluded spot)
secreti: sēcrētus, -a, -um — set apart, hidden, private (m./n. gen. sg.; m. nom. pl.)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedebant: sedeō, -ēre, sēdī, sessum — to sit, sit still (3rd pl. impf.)
sedes: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, settlement (acc./nom. pl.) · also nom. sg. (sēdēs fundātur)
sepulto: sepeliō, -īre, sepelīvī, sepultum — to bury (perf. pass. part., m./n. dat./abl. sg.: to the buried one)
servant: servō, -āre, -āvī — to save, keep safe, preserve (3rd pl. pres.)
servet: servō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to keep, save, guard (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
sibi: suī (reflexive pron.) — to/for himself, herself, themselves (dat.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
siste: sistō, -ere, stitī (stetī), statum — to cause to stand, set, bring (2nd sg. imper.)
sorte: sors, sortis (f.) — lot; allotment, portion, fate (abl. sg.)
stetit: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd sg. perf.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
suis: suus, -a, -um — his/her/its/their own (m./f./n. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.) · sūs, suis — pig (dat./abl. pl., rare)
sumere: sūmō, -ere, sumpsī, sumptum — to take, take up (pres. inf.; poenās sūmere, to exact vengeance)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō)
superos: superī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the gods above (acc. pl.)
suprema: suprēmus, -a, -um — highest, last, extreme (superl. of superus; f. nom./abl. sg.; n. pl.)
surgere: surgō, -ere, surrēxī — to rise, arise, grow (pres. inf.)
tales: tālis, -e — of such a kind, such (m./f. nom./acc. pl.; f. acc. pl., with cūrās)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tantae: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. gen./dat. sg.; f. nom. pl.)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tegit: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, shield (3rd sg. pres.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
tellure: tellūs, tellūris (f.) — earth, ground, land (abl. sg.)
tempora: tempus, temporis (n.) — time, season, occasion (acc. pl.) · also tempora, -um (n. pl.), temples of the head (acc. pl.)
tenebant: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd pl. impf.)
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
tenent: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, restrain (3rd pl. pres.)
tenentem: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, grasp, keep (pres. part., m. acc. sg.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tollere: tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise (pres. inf.)
torva: torvus, -a, -um — grim, fierce, savage (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
totoque: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (m./n. abl. sg.) + -que, and
trepidare: trepidō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to tremble, be in alarm (pres. inf., historic infinitive)
tris: trēs, tria — three (m./f. acc. pl., = trēs)
tristisque: tristis, -e — sad, grim (f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs) + -que 'and' · also f. nom. sg. (tristis senectūs)
tulit: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to bear, bring, carry; sē ferre, to betake oneself (3rd sg. perf.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumida: tumidus, -a, -um — swollen, surging (n. acc./nom. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
tumulum: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock, burial mound (acc. sg.)
ultima: ultimus, -a, -um — farthest, last, final; ultima, the last things (n. acc. pl. as noun; also f. nom./abl. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
ulva: ulva, -ae (f.) — sedge, marsh grass, reeds (abl. sg.)
undae: unda, -ae (f.) — wave, water (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
usque: usque (adv.) — all the way, continuously, ever, without ceasing
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
vasta: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (f. abl. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
venerat: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (3 sg. pluperf.)
veniendi: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (gerund, gen. sg.: of coming)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vertere: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change, drive (pres. inf.)
verus: vērus, -a, -um — true, real, genuine (m. nom. sg.)
veterem: vetus, veteris — old, ancient, long-standing (m./f. acc. sg.)
videre: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (pres. inf.)
videt: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. pres.)
vidisse: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (perf. inf.)
vim: vīs (f.; acc. vim, abl. vī) — force, power, violence (acc. sg.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
visum: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see; pass. to seem, seem good (perf. pass. part., n. nom. sg.; visum (est))
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
vocavi: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, call out to, summon (1st sg. perf.)
vocem: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, sound (acc. sg.)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
vocibus: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice; word, utterance (abl./dat. pl.)
